I farm the way I know best: I keep the wheat-maize rotation as the backbone of my land because it fits my fields, my labor, and my well irrigation. I am 66, my household is small, and I have farmed a long time, so I do not want a complicated plan. I will put 10 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will keep 5 mu in cotton because it spreads my risk and gives me another cash crop. For wheat and maize, I will use improved or hybrid seed, put on enough nitrogen to support yield, and use some phosphorus and potassium because I want steady production, not just low-cost input. Since I have well irrigation, I will irrigate the wheat more because it responds well and needs moisture at key stages, and I will irrigate maize and cotton fewer times. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical for me and suits my scale. I will spray pesticides only as much as needed to avoid losing yield, but I will not overdo it because labor and cost both matter to me. My goal is stable output from the wheat-maize land and dependable cash return from cotton.
